The sum of copywise Lagrangians is stationary and its Hessian is block diagonal. Its positive index is dN. Restricting a dN-dimensional positive subspace to the kernel of m linear constraints leaves dimension at least dN−m=d(N−1)−1≥1.

For a one-copy translation v1ᵀ with sum v_i=0, the column sums and trace are zero and row sums are mv_i. The cap derivative formula gives exactly the zero-sum cap subspace. For I−11ᵀ/m, the column and row sums vanish and its trace is d, giving a nonzero common derivative. Both are valid physical tangent matrices.

For B in the positive critical kernel, stationarity gives M′=0. For I+tB+t²C/2 the cap second derivative is its Hessian value plus the surjective first-derivative map applied to C, so it can be set to −ε in every row. The acceleration contributes zero to the stationary Lagrangian second derivative. M″ equals the positive Lagrangian Hessian value minus ε/γ, with γ=(d/m)^d. Positive and negative quadratic signs persist for all sufficiently small positive t.

The columns stay normalized, and the independent-neighborhood hypothesis ensures all small simultaneous vertex changes on the polynomial path satisfy actual compatibility. The theorem does not infer this feasibility from positive index alone.
